title: Optimal Therapies Through Data-Driven Decision-Making and Support Systems - Collaborative Project: Medical/HIS Subproject of TRANSFER
summary: During surgery, patients' blood pressure can drop to dangerous levels, potentially causing serious complications such as kidney failure, heart damage, or death. This study aims to develop an artificial intelligence system that can predict such blood pressure drops before they occur. To this end, existing routine treatment data from approximately 270,000 patients at Charité Berlin, collected between 2010 and 2026, will be analysed retrospectively. Additionally, a display interface will be developed to present the system's predictions to clinicians in a clear and practical way. This interface will be evaluated through interviews with medical staff.

interventions.name: Retrospective analysis of routine clinical data from approximately 270,000 patients (≥ 18 years, non-cardiac surgery with anaesthesiological involvement ≥ 30 min) at Charité – Universitätsmedizin Berlin, covering 01.01.2010–31.01.2026. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Non-cardiac surgical procedure with anaesthesiological involvement at Charité – Universitätsmedizin Berlin between 01.01.2010 and 31.01.2026; anaesthesia duration ≥ 30 minutes. For the UI development component: clinical staff (physicians).
Exclusion criteria:
For the retrospective data analysis: no exclusion criteria defined. For the UI development component: refusal to participate.
